content.purpose: Prove you can answer your own questions about an unfamiliar command.
content.mentalModel: Everything in this assessment is something you did in this module. There are no hints and no worked examples: the point is to find out what you can do unaided, which is the only measurement worth having.

remember: --help for a summary, man for the full reference, apropos when you do not know the name
type tells you what will actually run

tasks.instruction: Find the documentation for mkdir and save its one-line description to /home/student/answers/mkdir-description.txt. Create the answers directory if it does not exist.

validators.message: The file does not contain mkdir's description.

tasks.instruction: Determine whether cd is a program on disk or something built into the shell, and record the shell's own verdict in /home/student/answers/cd-verdict.txt.

validators.message: The file does not record that cd is a builtin.

tasks.instruction: Run a command you know will fail, and record its exit code in /home/student/answers/failure-code.txt. The file must contain a single non-zero number.

validators.message: The file does not contain a single non-zero exit code.

tasks.instruction: You do not know what command reports free disk space. Find it using a keyword search of the manual, and save the search results to /home/student/answers/disk-space-search.txt.

validators.message: The search results do not include a disk space command. Search the manual descriptions by keyword.

reviewQuestions.question: You meet a command you have never seen in a script. What is the fastest way to find out what it does?
answers: Run it with --help, or read whatis for a one-line summary
Run it and see what happens
reviewQuestions.explanation: Reading the documentation costs seconds. Running an unknown command from a script to find out what it does is how accidents happen.
